portraits.descricao: A living antique brass tram bell character named Trilim, for a Brazilian 2nd-grade educational comic book. Round and pot-bellied like an old-fashioned table bell, aged brass with a warm golden-purple sheen and soft verdigris patina in the grooves. A round expressive cartoon face is embossed on the metal belly: big glossy eyes, softly hammered brass eyebrows shaped like a tiny curled mustache, and the bell's internal clapper hangs out the bottom like a round little nose. Thin curved wire arms end in small three-fingered rounded brass hands, one arm raised in a warm friendly wave. No legs -- Trilim glides atop a small circular base shaped like two miniature curved train rails. On top of his head he wears a small triangular purple pennant flag. A purple-and-lilac plaid ribbon is tied around his neck where the bell narrows. Light scuffs and dents in the brass give him a lovingly-used charm. Full-body illustration, cheerful standing pose, big warm smile. Vibrant Brazilian children's educational comic book style, bold black outlines, clean cel-shading, bright saturated colors, exaggerated cartoonish chibi proportions, no sharp edges. Purple palette: primary #A855F7, light accent #D08EF8, brass tones #C9A05C and #7A4A12. Plain solid background, no scenery, no text, no speech bubbles, no other characters.
